references.text: Melchizedek blesses Abraham with 'God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth' – a direct parallel to Abraham's designation of God in his oath.
Esau takes wives from Canaanite peoples, causing grief for Isaac and Rebekah – exactly what Abraham sought to avoid for Isaac.
Isaac instructs Jacob not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, thus reflecting Abraham's instruction to his servant.
Moses forbids marriage with Canaanite peoples, in line with Abraham's desire to avoid such marriages.
God forbids making covenants and marrying with the peoples of Canaan, which reflects Abraham's principle of avoiding marriage with the Canaanites.
Abraham repeats his oath instruction to the servant: 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites.'
Both verses illustrate the recurring theological theme of protecting God's people from religious contamination through marriage with foreigners, from the patriarchal era until after the exile.
Ezekiel highlights the theological reason behind Abraham's requirement: to prevent God's people from being contaminated by pagan customs and idol worship.
